topic: The Mathematical Foundations of Bitcoin: Trust through Cryptography
target_audience: University students with a basic interest in computer science

sections.title: Introduction: The Digital Ledger
lecture_lines: Digital currency faces a double spending problem.
A shared ledger records all transactions securely.
Transactions are organized into chronological blocks.
animations: Display a chain graphic connecting blocks.
Zoom out to show the full structure.

sections.title: The Hash Function: The Digital Fingerprint
lecture_lines: SHA-256 creates a unique digital fingerprint.
Data transforms into a fixed-length hash.
The one-way property prevents reversing data.
animations: Show an input string transforming into a unique hash.

sections.title: Proof of Work: The Mathematical Puzzle
lecture_lines: Mining is a difficult computational lottery.
Miners guess a nonce for valid hashes.
Successful guessing adds a new block.
animations: Show successful solution finding block creation.
Add the block to the main chain.

sections.title: Public-Key Cryptography: Digital Signatures
lecture_lines: Users own a private key for signatures.
Public keys verify ownership without revealing secrets.
animations: Confirm integrity with a green checkmark.

sections.title: Synthesis: Chain Integrity
lecture_lines: Blocks link together using previous hashes.
Changing any block breaks the entire chain.
This design ensures total network integrity.
animations: Display the full chain of blocks.
Animate a tamper attempt detected with #E74C3C.
